prompt:
A student logs three entries in an experimental notebook: $A = 25$, $B = 25\text{ s}$, and $C = 25\text{ kg}$.
(a) Identify which record is scientifically incomplete, and explain why. [2]
(b) Explain why records B and C cannot be directly added together or compared in size, even though they have the identical numerical magnitude. [2]
answer:
(a) Record A is incomplete because it lacks a unit.
(b) Records B and C represent different physical quantities (time and mass) with different units. Only quantities of the same physical dimension can be added or compared.

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Explains that record A lacks a unit, so the scale / quantity is unknown.
(b) States that B is a time and C is a mass (or they have different units / represent different physical quantities).
(b) States that quantities with different dimensions/units cannot be added or directly compared.

hints: Which entry is missing its measurement scale?
Can you add 25 seconds to 25 kilograms?
solution:
(a) Record A is incomplete because it provides only a numerical magnitude (25) without any unit. Without a unit, the physical quantity and its scale cannot be determined.
(b) Record B represents a time interval (in seconds) while record C represents a mass (in kilograms). In physics, addition and direct size comparisons are only meaningful between quantities of the same physical kind and dimension. Time and mass are entirely distinct physical dimensions.
teacher_walkthrough: In part (a), allocate 1 mark for naming A and 1 mark for explaining the absence of the unit.
In part (b), allocate 1 mark for identifying the two different quantities (time vs mass) and 1 mark for explaining that differing dimensions cannot be added or compared.
